headline: Structure-aware models retain spatial and lineage dependence in single-cell analyses
label: Spatial Single Cell Omics Methods
summary: Per-cell analyses discard spatial, lineage, and ordering dependence that now shapes single-cell and spatial inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is retaining structure that standard per-cell analyses discard: spatial dependence in CDS, which scores directionality of structured interventions on spatial graphs with a Neighbor Influence Model and bootstrap uncertainty, and external condition ordering in SPARC, a shortest-path framework reconstructing directional trajectories. scDIV addresses diversity measurement robustly against graph-based clustering parameters. The osteosarcoma study pairs single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with mtDNA lineage tracing, placing COL3A1+ cells as the ancestral state under a WF-HMT model. The prostate study couples a cellular signaling model parameterized with TCGA and cBioPortal data to a spatial agent-based model. cellmig, a published R/Bioconductor tool, adds Bayesian hierarchical uncertainty quantification to live-cell migration velocity. What is new across these is explicit treatment of dependence in graph-based reconstruction and uncertainty quantification, though the items are heterogeneous and not every one addresses dependence directly.
